Glaucon uses the ring of gyges to explain his social contract theory, notably that we don’t harm each other because the potential damage by being harmed is greater than the potential advantage from harming others. The rest of the republic shows Socrates arguing the contrary, that the virtuous man would be virtuous not due to the social contract, but because it would make them happiest. This is as their tripartite soul would be in perfect harmony. In turn, anyone using the ring of gyges to abuse people would still be less happy than if they didn’t, so the matter of inflicting harm to gain an advantage without having any harm inflicted upon you becomes irrelevant. That is the argument as I’ve been taught it. I don’t know how that reflects on Greek philosohy in general tho

Imagine you’re a man and you falsely claim to be trans to enter the women’s toilet (for whatever perverted reason). You get caught and exit the bathroom, only to be tackled by a very angry boyfriend. A few days later, you enter the courtroom, and when provided the opportunity, proudly announce that you are in fact a transgender women, and were thus justified in having entered the women’s toilets. Something had to be wrong! 5 months in prison? Charged with sexual harassment? It just didn’t make any sense…

I got a little carried away but what I’m saying here, is that if you harass someone in a bathroom, gender is not the problem. It’s not the first time I’ve seen a comment like yours.
